get.description: Retrieve a page of CRM objects of a specified type. You can control the data returned by specifying properties, associations, and archived status. This endpoint is useful for fetching a list of objects with specific attributes and associations.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of objects that can be read by a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and return a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint is useful for adding new records to your CRM system. Documentation and examples for creating standard objects are provided.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects by their IDs. This endpoint is useful for moving multiple objects to the recycling bin in a single request, streamlining the process of managing large datasets.

Create a batch of CRM objects with the specified properties. This endpoint allows you to efficiently create multiple objects in a single request, returning a response that includes the details of the created objects. It's useful for bulk data operations where you need to add several objects at once.

Read a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint allows you to retrieve multiple objects in a single request, making it efficient for bulk data retrieval. It supports filtering for archived objects.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects of a specified type in a single request. It is useful for bulk updates, ensuring that all specified objects are updated consistently and efficiently.

Create or update a batch of CRM objects by unique property values. This endpoint allows you to efficiently manage multiple objects in one request, ensuring that existing objects are updated and new ones are created as needed.

Permanently delete a contact and all associated content to comply with GDPR regulations. This endpoint allows you to specify the contact by email address using the optional 'idProperty' set to 'email'. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist to prevent future use.

Merge two CRM objects of the same type in your HubSpot account. This operation combines the properties and associations of the specified objects into a single object, identified by the primary object ID. Use this endpoint to consolidate duplicate records and streamline data management.

Search for CRM objects of a specified type using the provided search criteria. This endpoint allows you to filter and sort objects based on various properties, making it useful for retrieving specific data sets from your CRM.

get.description: Read an object identified by `objectId`. By default, `objectId` refers to the internal object ID, but you can specify a unique property value using the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control the response content using the `properties` query parameter to include specific properties.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation effectively archives the object, making it no longer active but retrievable if needed.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an Object identified by `{objectId}`. `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. Provided property values will be overwritten. Read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties values can be cleared by passing an empty string.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type
